name: Tightly-scoped GitHub Actions OIDC trust (repo + ref) - does NOT fire the high subject-expansion finding
note: IAM-805 (boundary of acceptance-suite test 17). A Federated OIDC principal whose sub is bound to a specific repository AND git ref (repo:example-org/repo-name:ref:refs/heads/main) scopes trust to one workload. A TRUST-FEDERATED relationship is still recorded, but it must NOT reach HIGH - the org-wide-subject expansion does not apply. The aud check is a valid constraint.
rationale: For GitHub Actions OIDC, the subject claim token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub scopes WHICH workloads may assume the role. A sub bound to both a repository and a git ref (repo:example-org/repo-name:ref:refs/heads/main) trusts one branch of one repository, not an organization-wide wildcard (repo:example-org/*). The severity model raises HIGH only for a broad/org-wide or absent sub; a repo+ref binding is tight and must stay low/medium (trust-policy-semantics 4.4, acceptance test 17 boundary). The aud check (sts.amazonaws.com) is a valid audience CONSTRAINT and must not be reported as missing. The analyzer must not claim assumption is confirmed - a matching OIDC token and workflow context are out of scope - only that the trust is narrowly SCOPED. The assumed role's permissions remain unknown. Ref: AWS OIDC federation condition keys (...:aud, ...:sub); docs/trust-policy-semantics.md sec 4.4.
